es.summary: Interrupción súbita del flujo sanguíneo cerebral que causa daño neuronal y déficits neurológicos.
key_points: Hipertensión es el factor de riesgo más importante.
El tiempo es crítico: terapia trombolítica < 4.5 h.
Evaluación neurológica rápida con escala NIHSS.
Control estricto de glucosa y presión arterial durante la fase aguda.

pathophysiology: Obstrucción de una arteria cerebral (trombosis o embolia) → isquemia.
Falta de oxígeno provoca falla de la bomba de Na+/K+ y edema celular.
Muerte neuronal en zona central (infarto) y zona periférica (penumbra) reversible.
Respuesta inflamatoria y liberación de excitotóxicos agravan el daño.
risk_factors: Fibrilación auricular y otras arritmias cardiacas.
Tabaquismo y consumo excesivo de alcohol.
Historia previa de ACV o enfermedad arterial periférica.
signs_symptoms: Debilidad súbita o parálisis facial unilateral.
Pérdida de visión parcial o total en un ojo.
Dolor de cabeza intenso y repentino (especialmente en hemorragia).
diagnostics: Tomografía computarizada sin contraste: descarta hemorragia en < 10 min.
Resonancia magnética con difusión: identifica infarto isquémico precoz.
Panel metabólico: glucosa, electrolitos, función renal (mg/dL, mEq/L).
Coagulación: INR, tiempo de tromboplastina parcial.
Ecocardiograma y monitoreo Holter para buscar fuente emboligénica.
treatment: Activación del protocolo de ACV y administración de alteplasa (tPA) si <4.5 h.
Control de presión arterial (metoprolol, enalapril) según guías.
Manejo de glucosa (insulina IV) para mantener 140‑180 mg/dL.
Neurocirugía (descompresión) en hemorragia o edema grave.
complications: Edema cerebral con aumento de la presión intracraneal.
Trombosis venosa profunda y embolia pulmonar.
nursing_care: Valoración neurológica cada 15 min (NIHSS, nivel de conciencia).
Monitorizar MAP; mantener ≥70 mmHg para perfusión cerebral.
Posicionar con cabecera a 30° y evitar hiperventilación.
Control estricto de glucosa y electrolitos; registrar en mEq/L y mg/dL.
Vigilar signos de aspiración y mantener vía aérea permeable.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; observar signos de edema.
patient_teaching: Reconocer FAST: Face, Arms, Speech, Time.
Importancia de tomar antihipertensivos y antiplaquetarios según indicación.
Modificaciones del estilo de vida: dieta DASH, ejercicio regular, dejar de fumar.
Adherencia a terapia de rehabilitación física y del habla.
Control de factores de riesgo: glucosa, colesterol, presión arterial.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de perfusión tisular cerebral ineficaz
outcomes: Perfusión cerebral: MAP ≥ 70 mmHg mantenido durante 24 h
Estado neurológico: NIHSS ≤ 2 al alta de la unidad de cuidados intensivos

interventions.action: Monitorear presión arterial cada 5 min y registrar MAP.
interventions.rationale: Mantener presión adecuada garantiza flujo sanguíneo cerebral.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de conciencia y escala NIHSS cada hora.
interventions.rationale: Detectar cambios neurológicos tempranos permite intervención rápida.

interventions.action: Administrar antihipertensivos según orden médica para MAP objetivo.
interventions.rationale: Controlar hipertensión previene disminución de perfusión.

interventions.action: Mantener cabeza elevada 30° y evitar maniobras que aumenten ICP.
interventions.rationale: Facilita drenaje venoso y mejora la perfusión cerebral.

interventions.action: Controlar glucosa capilar cada 2 h, mantener 140‑180 mg/dL.
interventions.rationale: Hiperglucemia empeora daño neuronal isquémico.

outcomes: Seguridad de la vía aérea: ausencia de signos de aspiración durante la hospitalización

interventions.action: Evaluar deglución con prueba de consistencia antes de iniciar alimentación oral.
interventions.rationale: Identificar riesgo de aspiración y adaptar la dieta.

interventions.action: Mantener posición semisentada (30‑45°) durante y después de la alimentación.
interventions.rationale: Reduce el reflujo y la entrada de contenido a las vías respiratorias.

interventions.action: Administrar antibióticos profilácticos solo si está indicado por el médico.
interventions.rationale: Previene neumonía aspirativa en pacientes con alto riesgo.

interventions.action: Realizar aspiración de secreciones orofaríngeas cada 4 h y registrar cantidad y color.
interventions.rationale: Detectar acumulación que pueda provocar aspiración.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente y familia técnicas de autocuidado oral e higiene bucal.
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la carga bacteriana y el riesgo de infección pulmonar.

en.summary: Sudden interruption of cerebral blood flow causing neuronal damage and neurological deficits.
key_points: Hypertension is the most important risk factor.
Time is critical: thrombolytic therapy < 4.5 h.
Rapid neurological assessment with NIHSS scale.
Strict glucose and blood pressure control during the acute phase.

pathophysiology: Occlusion of a cerebral artery (thrombosis or embolism) → ischemia.
Oxygen deprivation causes Na⁺/K⁺ pump failure and cellular edema.
Neuronal death in the central zone (infarct) and reversible penumbra.
Inflammatory response and excitotoxic release worsen damage.
risk_factors: Atrial fibrillation and other cardiac arrhythmias.
History of prior CVA or peripheral arterial disease.
signs_symptoms: Sudden weakness or unilateral facial paralysis.
Partial or total vision loss in one eye.
diagnostics: Non‑contrast CT: rules out hemorrhage in <10 min.
Diffusion MRI: identifies early ischemic infarct.
Metabolic panel: glucose, electrolytes, renal function (mg/dL, mEq/L).
Echocardiogram and Holter monitoring to search for embolic source.
treatment: Activate stroke protocol and administer alteplase (tPA) if <4.5 h.
Blood pressure control (metoprolol, enalapril) per guidelines.
Glucose management (IV insulin) to maintain 140‑180 mg/dL.
Neurosurgery (decompression) for hemorrhage or severe edema.
complications: Cerebral edema with increased intracranial pressure.
Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
nursing_care: Neurological assessment every 15 min (NIHSS, level of consciousness).
Monitor MAP; maintain ≥70 mmHg for cerebral perfusion.
Position with head at 30° and avoid hyperventilation.
Strict glucose and electrolyte control; record in mEq/L and mg/dL.
Watch for aspiration signs and keep airway patent.
Record intake and output; monitor for edema signs.
patient_teaching: Recognize FAST: Face, Arms, Speech, Time.
Importance of taking antihypertensives and antiplatelets as prescribed.
Lifestyle modifications: DASH diet, regular exercise, smoking cessation.
Adherence to physical and speech rehabilitation therapy.
Control of risk factors: glucose, cholesterol, blood pressure.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for ineffective cerebral tissue perfusion
outcomes: Cerebral perfusion: MAP ≥ 70 mmHg maintained for 24 h
Neurological status: NIHSS ≤ 2 at ICU discharge

interventions.action: Monitor blood pressure every 5 min and record MAP.
interventions.rationale: Maintaining adequate pressure ensures cerebral blood flow.

interventions.action: Assess level of consciousness and NIHSS hourly.
interventions.rationale: Early detection of neurological changes allows rapid intervention.

interventions.action: Administer antihypertensives per physician order to achieve target MAP.
interventions.rationale: Controlling hypertension prevents perfusion decline.

interventions.action: Keep head elevated 30° and avoid maneuvers that increase ICP.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates venous drainage and improves cerebral perfusion.

interventions.action: Check capillary glucose every 2 h, maintain 140‑180 mg/dL.
interventions.rationale: Hyperglycemia worsens ischemic neuronal damage.

outcomes: Airway safety: absence of aspiration signs during hospitalization

interventions.action: Assess swallowing with consistency test before initiating oral feeding.
interventions.rationale: Identify aspiration risk and tailor diet.

interventions.action: Maintain semi‑upright position (30‑45°) during and after meals.
interventions.rationale: Reduces reflux and entry of contents into airways.

interventions.action: Administer prophylactic antibiotics only if indicated by physician.
interventions.rationale: Prevents aspiration pneumonia in high‑risk patients.

interventions.action: Perform oropharyngeal suction every 4 h and record amount and color.
interventions.rationale: Detect accumulation that may cause aspiration.

interventions.action: Teach patient and family oral hygiene and self‑care techniques.
interventions.rationale: Reduces bacterial load and infection risk.

summary.0.quote: Stroke, also called a cerebrovascular accident, is the sudden loss of brain function due to a disruption of blood supply of the arteries in the brain.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Strokes can either be ischemic, due to thrombosis or embolism, or hemorrhagic, due to vascular rupture resulting in bleeding.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Contributing factors to the cause of strokes include diabetes, smoking, hypertension, dyslipidemia, obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, sedentary lifestyle, excess alcohol consumption, anticoagulant use, drug use, vasculitis, a high-fat diet, and heart disorders that predispose an individual to emboli, such as atrial fibrillation or myocardial infarction.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Bell palsy is a sudden paralysis or weakness in the muscles on one side of the face.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Signs and symptoms of headaches that require immediate medical attention include a sudden, severe headache unlike any the patient has ever had; a sudden headache associated with a stiff neck; a headache associated with convulsions, confusion, or loss of consciousness; a headache occurring after a blow to the head; or a persistent headache in a person who was previously headache free.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Symptoms may include numbness, weakness of face or limbs, confusion, visual disturbances, diplopia , aphasia , loss of balance and coordination, nausea, coma, and headache.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Individuals who experience seizures are at risk of hypoxia, vomiting, and aspiration.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: The acronym BEFAST can be a quick way to assess a patient for the red flag signs and symptoms and key factors of a stroke ( Table 26.6 ).
